validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: confirmed real and correctly classified. This segment is the 'Lea County Expansion Project,' a ~20-mile, 20-inch lateral built by Carlsbad Gateway, LLC (a WhiteWater Midstream affiliate) under a FERC NGA Section 7 prior-notice/blanket-certificate filing (Docket CP24-200-000, filed 2024-04-19, Federal Register notice 2024-09688, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/05/03/2024-09688/carlsbad-gateway-llc-notice-of-request-under-blanket-authorization-and-establishing-intervention-and; verified via url_verifier, name_matched='Agua Blanca Pipeline'). It runs from the tailgate of Targa Resources' Red Hills Processing Plant in Lea County, New Mexico to an interconnection with the Agua Blanca Pipeline in Loving County, Texas -- exactly matching the sheet's segment name 'Targa Red Hills Interconnect.' NOTE TO DISPATCH BRIEF: the row was flagged as intrastate with FERC records expected thin/absent -- that expectation does NOT hold for this specific segment: Carlsbad Gateway holds an interstate NGA blanket certificate (Docket CP18-538-000) and filed this prior-notice request under it, so a full FERC/Federal Register record exists and is the strongest available source for this row. ROUTE CHECK: the routes-repo geojson for P7109 is internally labeled RouteName='Lea County Expansion', LineName='Carlsbad Gateway Pipeline' (not 'Agua Blanca'/'Targa Red Hills Interconnect') -- initially looked like a possible route/sheet mismatch. Resolved as NOT a mismatch: the route's first vertex (-103.5268, 32.2113) sits in Lea County, NM (matches the FERC-stated Red Hills Plant tailgate origin); its last vertex (-103.7092, 31.9878) sits in Loving County, TX (matches the FERC-stated Agua Blanca interconnection terminus); and the digitized length (20.07 mi) matches the FERC notice's 'approximately 20 miles.' The internal labels are the builder/operator's own project name for the same physical pipe, not a different asset -- route geometry is accurate, kept as-is. DUPLICATE CHECK: cross-checked against P7850 (Targa Forza / Bull Run Pipeline) -- both originate near the same Red Hills Plant area, but EIA's Aug2026 release (sheet 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects,' Excel row 53) lists Forza pipeline as a SEPARATE, larger project (Forza Pipeline LLC & Bull Run Pipeline LLC (Targa Resources), 36 mi, 36-inch, 750 MMcf/d, dockets CP26-34/CP26-35) with a different owner and a different docket than Carlsbad Gateway's 20-mile, 20-inch, 350,000 Dth/d CP24-200-000 project -- NOT a duplicate; see cross_row_leads. ATTRIBUTION CONCERN: the FERC notice names 'Carlsbad Gateway, LLC' as the filer/operator and gives its FERC contact as WhiteWater Midstream, LLC's own in-house senior counsel (Liza Evans) -- strong circumstantial evidence Carlsbad Gateway LLC is a WhiteWater Midstream affiliate, but this is an inference from corporate representation, not an explicit ownership disclosure. Checked Targa Resources' 10-Q (trgp-10q_20180630.htm) and MPLX's most recent 10-K Exhibit 21.1 subsidiary list for 'Carlsbad' -- zero hits in either, ruling OUT Carlsbad Gateway as a named Targa or MPLX subsidiary and as part of the 4-way Agua Blanca Joint Venture (WhiteWater/WPX-Devon/MPLX/Targa) that owns the mainline system. Staged Owner1='WhiteWater Midstream, LLC' at medium confidence/single-source with this caveat recorded in `contested`.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Cannot confirm OR contradict the recorded Status=operating with an independent, currently-dated, citable source. The only verified independent evidence (FERC Federal Register notice, filed 2024-04-19) shows only the AUTHORIZATION stage as of April 2024, over two years before this sweep (2026-09-14) -- plausible that construction has since completed and the line is now operating, but nothing citable confirms it. The sheet's own current_ref (whitewatermidstream.com/projects) is an unverifiable client-rendered SPA shell with no server-side content (curl-confirmed, 1669 bytes). The routes-repo geojson carries a non-citable internal property suggesting a ~2024-12-31 target in-service date, consistent with 'now operating' but not usable as a public ref. Search for a completion/in-service announcement (FERC eLibrary, PHMSA NPMS, NGI, Hart Energy, Businesswire, SEC EDGAR full-text, general web search) came up blocked/inaccessible/empty or budget-exhausted (see Status fill notes). Verdict left 'unclear' rather than 'confirm' or 'change' -- staging either would assert more than the evidence supports, and the fills[Status] record is deliberately left UNRESOLVED to avoid contradicting this verdict.

summary: P7109 Agua Blanca Pipeline / Targa Red Hills Interconnect confirmed real and correctly located: it is Carlsbad Gateway LLC's (WhiteWater Midstream affiliate) 'Lea County Expansion Project,' a ~20 mi/20 in lateral from Targa's Red Hills Processing Plant (Lea County, NM) to the Agua Blanca Pipeline (Loving County, TX), sourced almost entirely to one strong primary record: FERC Docket CP24-200-000 / Federal Register notice 2024-09688 (filed 2024-04-19). Route geojson's internal 'Carlsbad Gateway'/'Lea County Expansion' labels initially looked like a mismatch but are confirmed the same physical pipe, geometry accurate. Ruled out as a duplicate of P7850 (Targa Forza/Bull Run, a separate, larger, Targa-owned project -- see cross_row_leads). One attribution concern staged (Owner1='WhiteWater Midstream, LLC' is a medium-confidence inference from the FERC filing's in-house-counsel contact, not an explicit ownership disclosure). 15/15 worklist units covered: 11 REFS_ADDED (Fuel, PipelineType, Proposal, Capacity, Length, Diameter, FuelSource, Location, SegmentCost, Operator, Owner), 4 UNRESOLVED (Construction, Start, Pressure, and Status -- Status intentionally left UNRESOLVED rather than confirmed, since the only verified source proves 2024-04 authorization-stage only, not current operating status; status_reviews verdict='unclear' for the same reason, not contradicting fills[Status]).
